original_question: Is there a combinatorial description, analogous to the one known in the ordinary Jack-polynomial setting, for the coefficients v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) appearing in the monomial expansion J^(alpha)_Lambda = sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega of integral-form Jack superpolynomials?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the review’s open-problem discussion around the integral-form Jack/Macdonald superpolynomials, specifically the superspace analogue of the ordinary Jack integral-form coefficient problem: to obtain an explicit combinatorial formula for the monomial coefficients of the integral-form Jack superpolynomials, equivalently the conjectural positivity/integrality statement that these coefficients should admit a Jack-style combinatorial description. In the literature summarized by the review, this is the Jack-side problem underlying the later q,t-version formulated as Conjecture 3 for Macdonald superpolynomials.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right family of objects (integral-form Jack superpolynomials), the right coefficients (the monomial-basis coefficients v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha)), and the right kind of question (a superspace analogue of the ordinary Jack-polynomial combinatorial formula). It also stays narrowly focused on the monomial expansion rather than drifting to broader positivity or representation-theoretic problems.
missing_details: It does not specify the ambient ring: symmetric superpolynomials in commuting variables x=(x_1,x_2,...) and anticommuting variables theta=(theta_1,theta_2,...) with theta_i theta_j = - theta_j theta_i and theta_i^2 = 0.
It does not say that Lambda and Omega are superpartitions of the same bi-degree (bosonic degree n and fermionic degree m).
It does not define m_Omega as the monomial superfunction basis.
It does not define the order Omega <= Lambda, which in this setting is the superpartition dominance/triangularity order used for Jack superpolynomials in superspace.

It does not state the normalization defining the integral form, namely that J_Lambda^(alpha) is a specific scalar multiple of P_Lambda^(alpha), usually written J_Lambda^(alpha)=v_Lambda(alpha) P_Lambda^(alpha).
It does not say whether the goal is merely existence of some combinatorial description, or the sharper paper-faithful aim: an explicit Jack-style formula proving coefficient integrality/positivity.

It does not state the expected coefficient ring: the paper-faithful target is not an arbitrary description, but a formula yielding polynomial coefficients in alpha, and in the Jack setting the natural sharpened expectation is positivity/integrality analogous to the ordinary Knop-Sahi-type formula.

It does not mention the finite-N/stable interpretation: these superpolynomials are first defined in N commuting and N anticommuting variables and then stabilize; one should at least indicate that N is sufficiently large for Lambda.
It does not make explicit that the question is for all superpartitions Lambda and all Omega <= Lambda.
It does not indicate that this problem is the Jack-side precursor of the integral-form Macdonald-superpolynomial conjecture discussed nearby in the same review literature.
refined_question: Let Lambda be a superpartition of bosonic degree n and fermionic degree m, and let P_Lambda^(alpha) be the Jack superpolynomial in the ring of symmetric superpolynomials in commuting variables x and anticommuting variables theta (with theta_i theta_j = -theta_j theta_i and theta_i^2=0), taken in the stable range of sufficiently many variables. If J_Lambda^(alpha)=v_Lambda(alpha) P_Lambda^(alpha) denotes its integral form and one writes its triangular monomial expansion as J_Lambda^(alpha)=sum_{Omega <= Lambda} v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha) m_Omega, where m_Omega is the monomial superfunction basis and <= is the standard superpartition order, is there a superspace analogue of the ordinary Jack Knop-Sahi-type combinatorial formula giving an explicit combinatorial expression for every coefficient v_{Lambda,Omega}(alpha), in particular one that proves the expected polynomial integrality/positivity of these coefficients in alpha for all Omega <= Lambda?
justification: The draft is close to the paper’s intent because it singles out the integral-form Jack superpolynomials and their monomial coefficients. What it misses is that, in the review literature being summarized, this is not posed as a loose request for any combinatorial description: it is the superspace analogue of the ordinary Jack integral-form coefficient problem, whose sharpened content is an explicit Jack-style combinatorial rule strong enough to force polynomial integrality/positivity of the coefficients. The review itself is a compendium and points back to the original conjectural sources; the nearest official formulation that can be pinned down from the cited literature is the Macdonald-superpolynomial integral-form conjecture (Conjecture 3), explicitly described there as the q,t-version of the earlier Jack conjecture. So the refined question should mention the superspace ring, superpartitions, monomial superfunctions, the triangular order, the integral-form normalization, the quantifier over all Lambda and Omega<=Lambda, and the intended positivity/integrality strength of the sought combinatorial formula.
